subject: Tenant 32k-window throughput & tail latency surge — urgent escalation
messages:
From: Jesse Alvarez <jesse@acmehealth.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 05 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0000
Subject: Hosted API: sudden p99 spikes on 32k requests - urgent

Hi Connor,

We started seeing a sustained jump in p95/p99 latency for our long-context generation jobs late last night (approx 23:40 PST on 2026-12-04). This is specifically visible for requests that pass ~30k-32k token windows; p99 has moved from ~1.1s to ~8-12s and we are also seeing intermittent 504s and a small spike in 500s (~1.2% of requests). Throughput for our tenant has dropped by ~25% as batch queues back up.

Examples: request IDs 8a3f2c4, 8a3f2c9; timestamps attached in the log. We are on the Hosted API (prod tenant: acme-health-prod) and this is impacting last-night batch scoring and some live inference.

We need immediate mitigation (reduce failed requests and bring p99 back down) and a clear timeline for full resolution. If this requires an exec-level engagement/credit discussion please escalate — this is customer-impacting for multiple product teams here.

Attached: acme_session_logs_20261204.log (snips with request IDs), a short sample prompt that reproduces the high tail latency.

Thanks,
Jesse
Director of ML Eng
Acme Health
From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jesse Alvarez <jesse@acmehealth.com>
Date: Sat, 05 Dec 2026 09:40:00 -0000
Subject: RE: Hosted API: sudden p99 spikes on 32k requests - urgent

Team — Jesse from Acme Health (prod tenant acme-health-prod) has hit a large p95/p99 regression on their long-window requests (30k-32k). They report increased 500s and some 504s; throughput is down for that tenant.

Initial notes from quick look:
- Spike appears correlated with increased long-prefix KV cache misses and very large effective batch sizes when the scheduler groups long-context requests.
- We are seeing queue growth on the gpu-serving topology for region us-east-1; per-tenant concurrency may be triggering head-of-line blocking.

Ask: marissa, can you triage the serving queues/traces and propose an immediate mitigation we can apply for this tenant (throttle/limit-context/max_prefix or force smaller batch size)? laura, pls sanity-check whether a rollback to the last-known-quantized variant is safe here. neha, please prepare a customer-facing mitigation note and credit/timeframe options if requested. markus, heads-up so this can be escalated to ops/exec if SLA credits are required.

I will coordinate with Acme on a short call if needed. Linked trace: https://console.aws.amazon.com/cloudwatch/home?region=us-east-1#logsV2:log-groups/log-group/$252Fredwood%252Facme-tenant

- Connor
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 05 Dec 2026 11:05:00 -0000
Subject: RE: Tenant 32k-window throughput & tail latency surge — triage notes

Connor / all,

Quick triage summary (initial):
- Evidence shows an uptick in KV cache misses for long-prefix requests starting 2026-12-04 23:20 PST. When cache miss rate spikes for large contexts the runtime ends up replaying more KV loads and the scheduler increases batch size heuristically which leads to head-of-line blocking on a subset of GPU workers.
- On a few workers we observed repeated small retried tasks and transient OOMs (no persistent node death) that triggered backoff/requeue (~3-4s extra per retry).
- Error-rate bump (500s) correlates with those retries and the external 504s come from the api-gateway timeout while worker backlog grows.

Immediate mitigations (recommended, low-risk):
1) Per-tenant policy: set max_context_tokens to 16000 for acme-health-prod (quick config change) — should prevent the 32k windows from entering the long-path codegen.
2) Apply temporary per-tenant throttle: max_concurrent_inference=6 for this tenant to reduce queue depth.
3) Disable inter-request auto-batching for acme-health-prod for 2 hours while we monitor (scheduler flag).
4) If the above doesn't stabilize p99 within 30-45 minutes, revert to the previous model variant (model-v2q-small) for that tenant (safe rollback tested earlier this year).

I can push the config changes now if we sign off. I will also capture a targeted flamegraph and upload a trimmed trace (acme_topology_trace_1205.json).

- Marissa
SRE, Redwood Inference

Connor / Marissa,

Thanks for the quick replies and proposed mitigations. We asked our infra team to avoid hitting the long-window path while you apply changes. We lifted traffic after 11:45 PST and saw immediate improvement, but over the next hour a subset of our jobs still surfaced 500s (new request IDs attached in the log).

We need:
- Confirmation of which mitigations were applied and timestamps.
- If you plan to throttle us, what is the expected RPS and for how long?
- A timeline for full resolution; if rollback is required we need the window/downtime expectations.
- Given the customer-impacting nature—we will need to discuss credits if SLA targets are missed.

Please escalate to execs if necessary; CC'd our CFO given the business impact.

Best,
Ana

Acme Health

From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 07 Dec 2026 08:15:00 -0000
Subject: RE: Tenant 32k-window throughput & tail latency surge — mitigation plan and next steps

Ana / Jesse —

Thanks for the patience. Quick status and plan:

What we applied (timestamps UTC):
- 2026-12-05T11:20Z: applied per-tenant policy max_context_tokens=16000 (acme-health-prod) — immediate partial improvement in tail latency.
- 2026-12-05T11:24Z: applied temporary throttle max_concurrent_inference=6 (expected RPS approx 12-15 for your typical payloads).
- 2026-12-05T11:30Z: disabled inter-request auto-batching for the tenant for monitoring window.
- 2026-12-05T12:15Z: rolled back to model-v2q-small in a canary (10% of traffic) — no regressions observed; can expand if stable.

Observed outcome: p99 dropped from 8-12s down to ~1.6-2.4s within the first 30 minutes for the majority of jobs; a small fraction (~0.3%) continued to see 500s while we tracked down a retry race condition.

Next steps (immediate):
- Marissa to run targeted runbook to close the retry race and deploy a patch to the scheduler by 2026-12-07T18:00Z.
- If patch is stable we will re-enable controlled batching and gradually return max_context_tokens for the tenant in staged increments.
- Postmortem and customer-facing incident report targeted for 2026-12-10.

Credits / commercial note: Neha — can you draft the credit proposal for Acme (based on impacted windows) and propose a goodwill package? I recommend a pro-rated credit plus a free month of dedicated support while we stabilize.

Attached: mutual_action_plan_acme_20261207.pdf (M.A.P with timeline, rollback plan and contact list).

I will set up a 30-minute exec call today at 18:00 PST so we can walk through the technical findings and the remediation timeline. Please let me know if that time doesn't work.

- Connor
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
